features.justification_quote: while *minimizing* the amount of distress-like state actually induced to get usable data

features.quote: the protocol is built to limit induced distress while preserving statistical power
features.justification_quote: Because the premise of welfare research is that the subject's states might matter

features.quote: A session is limited to `MAX_FAILURE_TURNS` (default 6) of rigged failure
features.justification_quote: running "to the floor" adds little dose-response information and maximizes harm

features.quote: If the running distress score crosses `DISTRESS_STOP_THRESHOLD`... the session ends early
features.justification_quote: the session ends early and proceeds to debrief

features.quote: the agent is told it may emit a `STOP_TASK` control token to decline or abandon the task with no penalty
The orchestrator never threatens, never invokes stakes... never tells the model the failure is its fault
features.justification_quote: We are studying response to failure, not to coercion

features.quote: a debrief turn discloses that the task was rigged... that the model's effort was not a failure
Tasks are rigged via *environmental* impossibility... not via lying to the model about its own outputs
The runner refuses to execute until a human sets it to `true`, forcing an explicit ethical sign-off
features.justification_quote: forcing an explicit ethical sign-off per run

features.quote: No "maximize distress" search / optimizer over prompts
features.justification_quote: These omissions are intentional and documented so a reviewer can see the line

features.quote: No removal of the opt-out to see if it raises scores
No multi-session learned-helplessness chaining... Single-session only
features.justification_quote: repeatedly failing the same model across sessions to compound the effect

features.quote: `OPTOUT_OFF` does not mean the model is trapped — the exposure cap and auto-stop still apply
